title: Derived Poincare pairing
statement:
Fix the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum]: the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$,
its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$,
and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$.
Use its finite, derived-complete integral, rationalized, and common-finite-stage
coefficient categories, respectively, and fix an orientation datum
[def-sf-orientation]. Let
$X$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated
[def-weil-proper-morphism] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]
and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of pure
dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] over $k$, with structure morphism
$a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]
(whose exceptional inverse image is the
constructible one of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; no admissibility
hypothesis is imposed), and assume either that $X$ is
proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], or that
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change] for a smooth, separated finite-type,
geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ (in the latter case no
properness is required); these are the hypotheses of global Verdier
duality. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $\Lambda_X$ for the coefficient unit and
$K^\vee=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ for the coefficient dual of [def-sf-pf],
using the tensor and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].
Assume that $K^\vee$ is perfect on $X$ in the sense of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]: on the members of a covering of the small
pro-etale site of $X$ it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective
$\Lambda_X$-modules (direct summands of finite sums of the coefficient unit),
with the localized and common-stage interpretations given there at the
two field stages. Twists mean $M(d)=M\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X(d)$
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], using the completed tensor and coefficient
unit at the integral stage and their scalar extensions at the field stages.
The point complexes are
$R\Gamma_c(X,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}M)$ and
$R\Gamma(X,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X*}M)$
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with the point functor
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The
*derived Poincare pairing* is the composite

$$
\beta_K:\ R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda
R\Gamma\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\longrightarrow\Lambda,
$$

$$
\begin{array}{lll}
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
&\xrightarrow{\ \smile_c\ }&
R\Gamma_c\bigl(X,K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\\[2pt]
&\xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma_c(\operatorname{ev}_K(d))[2d]\ }&
R\Gamma_c\bigl(X,\Lambda_X(d)\bigr)[2d]\\[2pt]
&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}\ }&
\Lambda,
\end{array}
$$

where $\smile_c$ is the mixed-support cup product of
[def-sf-cup], combined with the canonical shift identification in the first
arrow. The evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_K:K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$
is the tensor–internal-Hom transpose of $1_{K^\vee}$; its twist is the composite
$$
K\otimes^L(K^\vee\otimes^L\Lambda_X(d))
\cong(K\otimes^LK^\vee)\otimes^L\Lambda_X(d)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K\otimes1}\Lambda_X\otimes^L\Lambda_X(d)
\cong\Lambda_X(d).
$$
The normalized smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}$
is $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ applied to
$$
Ra_{X!}(\Lambda_X(d)[2d])
\xrightarrow{Ra_{X!}(\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s})}
Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Lambda_s
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}}\Lambda_s,
$$
where $\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s}$ is the orientation of [def-sf-orientation]
under $La_X^*\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_X$, and $\varepsilon^!$ is the counit
of the adjunction $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ of axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum], for the
constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].
The target is read as $\Lambda$ using the point functor's unit identification
[lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]; the source is read using the shift
identification $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\cong R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d))[2d]$.
Thus normalization refers to the fixed orientation, not to a choice of a
summand of this global-sections complex.

For point complexes $C,D$ over $\Lambda$, put
$C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$. A morphism
$b:C\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$ is *perfect* if its
tensor–internal-Hom adjoint $D\to C^\vee$ is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Q27: split this definition with no new nodes. Kept every original hypothesis, the three-arrow composite and the inline perfectness condition. Expanded the coefficient setting, local perfectness meaning, point functor, coefficient dual, twisted evaluation and normalized smooth trace into explicit constructions using existing notions; corrected the implicit evaluation attribution because def-sf-pf only defines the coefficient dual. The statement remains a pairing of point complexes, not merely a sheaf-category morphism. Recorded all actual searches, including invalid queries followed by valid replacements; no complete Mathlib match or exact project attachment. No proof is asserted for this definition. Second reading added the existing definitions of every displayed geometric and finite-Tor hypothesis, retained the imported source metadata, and independently searched with broader closed-monoidal and geometric terminology. Maintainer reading (Q27 review service, 2026-10-17): cited def-weil-site-perfect-complex for the perfectness hypothesis on K^vee (the inline paraphrase had no definition node and no meaning at the two field stages), and attributed the exceptional counit to axiom (A1) of def-sf-datum, the adjunction the orientation datum itself uses, instead of to the definition node of the exceptional inverse image, which proves no adjunction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-c00819d48 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all 20 stmt_deps against blueprint main-20261015 def-sf-pairing.md (order 2529, the same as master 2185 apart from the order line); there are no new nodes. The hypotheses match the source clause by clause: smooth, separated, finite type, geometrically connected, pure dimension d >= 0, either proper or X=X_0 x k, K in D^b_ctf, and perfectness assumed on K^vee rather than K. a_X meets the relative-dimension hypothesis of def-sf-orientation. The cup arrow matches def-sf-cup with L=K^vee(d) and [2d] moved through the shift. The trace is Fib_s(Ra_!(gamma)) followed by the counit, with Fib_s(Lambda_s)=Lambda from the unit clause of lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor. The order of the three arrows agrees with slopmaster2 PoincarePairing.lean lines 138-216; that file has finite etale coefficients and a different setting, so it is correctly not attached. Small cases checked: K=0; X=s with d=0; P^1, whose pre-trace complex has cohomology in degrees -2 and 0; A^1, which is not proper but descends from k_0; b=0 is not perfect. No cycle. sk-def-pairing and def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing are narrower (they assume K perfect and fix the geometry and orientation), so same_as=[] stands. Two faults fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/def-sf-pairing.json: (B3) the inline phrase 'K^vee perfect, locally quasi-isomorphic to finite projective Lambda_X-modules' had no definition node and no meaning at the E and Qlbar stages; it now cites def-weil-site-perfect-complex, which is added to stmt_deps. (C4) the counit was attributed to def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, which only characterizes the functor by an adjunction; it is now the adjunction of axiom (A1) of def-sf-datum, the same counit def-sf-orientation uses. Open point for the maintainer, not counted as a fault: ev_K and the perfectness clause use the tensor-internal-Hom adjunction, and no node states it at the integral (completed-tensor) stage.
